note: Unit 19 assignment tasks in plain language, based on the centre's 2025-26 assignment briefs and the Pearson Unit 19 assessment guidance. Used by the Assignment guide, the Assignment builder and the AI assignment coach.

assignments.title: Assignment 1: Investigating computer networks
assignments.scenario: You are a junior network technician at a company that designs and installs networks. The company publishes detailed technical pages on its website to help new and existing customers understand networks.
assignments.evidence: A report (written as website pages and a table)

tasks.title: Website pages: why different network types and models are needed
tasks.asks: Explain why organisations need each network type (LAN, WLAN, WAN, SAN, intranet, extranet, internet, cloud, wired and wireless integration) and how those needs affect the choice of network model (peer-to-peer, client/server, thin client). Include why protocols and standards matter, why different topologies are used, and current trends such as BYOD and cloud computing.
checklist: Every network type is explained with a clear reason why an organisation would need it
Each type has a realistic example organisation or situation
Peer-to-peer, client/server and thin client are explained, and you show how an organisation's needs decide which model it chooses
Topologies are covered, with why different ones are used
You explain why protocols and standards (e.g. IEEE 802, TCP/IP) are needed to connect different networks
Current trends are included: at least BYOD and cloud, ideally virtualisation and SDN too
It is written for a customer reading a website: clear headings, plain explanations of technical terms
It is in your own words, with any sources referenced

tasks.title: Table: functions and characteristics of network components
tasks.asks: Create a table explaining the general functions and characteristics of the hardware and software used to build and connect networks: end user devices (including mobile), switches, routers, access points; cable, wireless and fibre media; networking systems software, monitoring/management/troubleshooting tools, and network applications.
checklist: Every hardware item is included: end devices (including mobile), switch, router, access point
Every media type is included: copper cable, wireless, fibre
Every software type is included: systems software, monitoring/management/troubleshooting tools, network applications
For each item you give its function (what it does)
For each item you give its characteristics (features you would compare, e.g. speed, ports, range, cost)
Examples are given for the software tools (e.g. ping, Wireshark, Event Viewer)

tasks.title: Report: analysing how the components work together
tasks.asks: Using your table, write a report that thoroughly analyses the key functions of the hardware and software components, including those used in LAN, WAN and wireless networks. Show accurate understanding of why protocols and standards are needed to connect different networks, with examples and illustrations of how data is transferred within and between networks.
checklist: You go beyond describing: you explain how and why each component is needed and how components depend on each other
LAN, WAN and wireless networks are all covered
You explain the importance of protocols and standards with specific examples (e.g. Ethernet, 802.11, IP, TCP, DNS, DHCP)
You illustrate data moving within a network (e.g. switch using MAC addresses) and between networks (e.g. router using IP addresses)
Diagrams or illustrations support your explanation
Technical terms are used accurately

tasks.title: Report: evaluating network models for different clients
tasks.asks: Write a clear and balanced evaluation of peer-to-peer, client/server and thin client models and their suitability for different client requirements. Consider ease of use, ease of set-up, performance and suitability for different kinds of applications, with reasoned examples, benefits and drawbacks.
checklist: All three models are evaluated
Each model has both benefits and drawbacks
You compare them on ease of use, ease of set-up, performance and suitability for different applications
Every point is supported with a reasoned example of a realistic client
Your reasoning is connected (because… therefore… however…)
You reach a justified conclusion about which model suits which kind of client
Accurate, fluent technical vocabulary and a clear structure

assignments.title: Assignment 2: Design, build, test and evaluate a network
assignments.scenario: You are a junior network engineer. Your supervisor has asked you to design, install, test and evaluate a network for a small branch office of a customer that creates web designs.
requirements: A server providing DHCP, DNS and web services
A wired network plus secure Wi-Fi
Internet access, and a router connection between both sites (one off-site office)
Suitable networking equipment, and an inventory of it
Users and groups with folder permissions as specified in the brief's table (HR, ADMIN and IT_SERVICES groups; you own all folders)
Scalable and secure for the future
Full documentation including test plans and results
assignments.evidence: Customer email; design documentation; written justification; implementation evidence (screenshots, photos); test evidence; evaluation; self-management portfolio

tasks.title: Email to the customer: why design and planning come first
tasks.asks: Write a professional email to the customer explaining why a network design and planning strategies are needed before installation, and how they make sure the network meets the organisation's needs and design goals.
checklist: Written as a professional email for a non-technical customer
Explains the purpose of a network design and of planning strategies
Links design and planning to the customer's needs and business goals
Mentions design goals such as scalability, availability, security and cost
Explains the risks of installing without a plan
Clear, polite tone with technical terms explained

tasks.title: Network design for the customer
tasks.asks: Design a network that meets the customer's requirements, including their goals and technical requirements, design aims and constraints; a physical design with component selection, network diagrams and physical layout; and a logical design with IP addressing and naming schemes.
checklist: Organisation goals and technical requirements are listed
Design aims and constraints (budget, time, environment) are stated
Equipment is selected with a reason for each item, and an inventory is included
A physical layout shows where equipment and cables go in the office
A network diagram shows every device and connection at both sites
A logical design gives an IP addressing table (networks, masks, gateways, static and DHCP ranges)
A naming scheme is used for devices
Users, groups and folder permissions from the brief are planned
Every requirement in the brief is covered somewhere in the design

tasks.title: Justification of your design decisions
tasks.asks: Justify the design decisions you made, referring both to technical considerations and to the customer's requirements, showing how the design fulfils its purpose.
checklist: Each major decision is justified: topology, devices, media, addressing, services, security, wireless
Every justification links to a specific customer requirement
Every justification also gives a technical reason
Alternatives you rejected are mentioned, with why
Trade-offs (cost versus performance or security) are explained

tasks.title: Build and configure the network
tasks.asks: Develop, set up and configure the network following your design, including devices, services, users, groups and permissions.
checklist: The network is built to match your design (both sites)
Router and switch configurations are done (names, addresses, routes, passwords)
Server services are configured: DHCP, DNS and web
Wireless is configured with security
VoIP, antivirus and e-commerce facilities are addressed
Users, groups and permissions are created as specified
All network devices are password protected
Screenshots or photos show each stage, with captions

tasks.title: Test the network, then optimise it
tasks.asks: Test the network using a completed test plan to make sure the functions the customer requires work. Then optimise the network to improve its performance, functionality or ease of use, based on your testing.
checklist: The test plan covers connectivity, services, access and security
Each test has the method, expected result, actual result and pass/fail
Evidence (screenshots) is referenced for each test
Failed tests are recorded with the cause and the fix, then re-tested
Merit: at least one optimisation is made because of what testing showed
Merit: re-testing proves the optimisation improved performance, security or usability

tasks.title: Review and evaluate the network against the requirements
tasks.asks: Review how far the network meets the client requirements. For Distinction, evaluate both the design and the implemented, optimised network against the requirements, using evidence from all stages, reaching conclusions and suggesting future developments.
checklist: Every client requirement is reviewed: met, partly met or not met
Positive and negative points are included
Distinction: the design and the implementation are both evaluated
Distinction: evidence is used from design, build, testing and optimisation
Distinction: you explain why things worked or did not
Distinction: justified conclusions and realistic future developments

tasks.title: Portfolio: individual responsibility and self-management
tasks.asks: Throughout the assignment, show individual responsibility and effective self-management in planning and implementing the network, through a portfolio.
checklist: A plan with targets and deadlines, updated as you go
Dated diary or log entries throughout the project
Peer feedback gathered on your design, and what you changed as a result
Evidence of professional behaviour: meeting deadlines, supporting others
Problems you met and how you solved them
Clear, professional communication in all documents
